label: copy-phase re-input of k or p (sparse tail, long sequences)
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (99.7% of mass) when the fed-back input token is k (68% of mass) or p (28%). It never fires at the delimiter and almost never in the original phase. Within that condition it is extremely sparse: about 0.5% of copy-phase k/p steps activate, so precision is very low (dev P=0.005, R=0.95, mass recall 0.96). Activation is concentrated in long sequences (L=9 holds 63% of mass, none for L<=4) and in late copy steps (rate rises with t and recall_idx). It is enriched when the previous input is c, 3 or t (lift 6-9x), and when the token being output is p, 2, k, a, o or m. Stacking these conditions raised dev F1 only to 0.24 (P=0.18, R=0.36), so the remaining selectivity is a diffuse conjunction of context that I could not capture. Magnitudes are small and fairly uniform (median 0.12, max 0.25), and I did not find a variable that clearly modulates them. It does not fire on first occurrences of tokens or on other letters or digits.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=k (+7.05), phase=2 & in_tok=p (+6.02), prev_tok=c (+3.57), prev_tok=3 (+3.48), prev_tok=t (+3.34), phase=2 & out_tok=2 (+2.97). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.43), orig0=p (-2.09), prev2_tok=w (-1.71), orig5=- (-1.47).
